ShortDescription.Value: Build one city together over a dedicated server. Roads, zoning, terrain, policies, progression and mod settings sync live; a small server program holds the shared city on your PC or on a Linux box.

Publish.LongDescription:
Build one city with friends. A small server program holds the shared city and passes round what everyone does; the game talks to it through this mod. Run the server from your own PC with one click, or put it on a Linux or Windows box and leave it running for your group.
**What syncs live** - Roads, buildings, zoning, bulldozing, terrain, districts and transit lines appear on everyone's screen as they are placed. You also see the other players' tool ghosts: the road they are dragging out, the building under their cursor, the area they are drawing. - Taxes, budgets, service fees, city policies and building options. - Progression: a development node one player buys is bought for everyone, and the host's XP and development points are shared, so milestones arrive together. - One treasury. The host's balance is the city's balance. - Where everyone is: a ring where each player is looking, a dot under their mouse, their name over it. - Other mods' settings: Traffic Tool Essentials junction settings, the Traffic mod's lane connections and priority signs, and Road Builder's custom roads.
Farms, forestry, mines and oil fields are the one thing not sent live yet; they arrive with the next save.
**How a session works** Main menu > **Multiplayer**. **Host game** starts the server window next to your game and joins it; friends join your address and port (27015 unless you change it, forwarded on your router). **Join game** connects to a friend or to a dedicated server. Joining from the menu downloads the shared city and loads it.
In a city, the round button at the top of the right-hand stack opens the panel: save to the server, fetch the newer city, see who is on. Anyone can save. The host also saves on its own every few minutes, and whoever joins later gets the latest save.
When the host connects and the server already holds a city, the game asks: load last save, or new world. New world opens the map list, mod maps included, and the city you start replaces the one on the server.
The simulation itself still runs on each PC, so citizens and traffic are not identical everywhere. Everything you build is.
**Dedicated server** This is a dedicated-server mod. The server is a separate program, not the game, so it runs on a box without Cities: Skylines II installed. The same program that Host game opens is on GitHub as a download for Linux and Windows, with an install script that sets it up as a service. All settings sit in one server.json file (name, password, owner key, mod check, welcome message) and the server picks up edits on its own. It can follow a public Paradox playset and tell anyone it turns away exactly which mods they are missing, and it checks GitHub for newer releases.
Server downloads, source code and issues: github.com/DillanStephenson/Cities-Skylines-2---multiplayer-DEDICATED-SERVER
**Mods** Any mod is fine as long as everyone runs the same playset. The server compares mod lists, ignoring version numbers, and tells a rejected player which playset to activate.
**Credits** Made by Dillan Stephenson. Testing: Mayor William. Thanks to the makers of Traffic Tool Essentials, Traffic and Road Builder, whose mods this one learned to carry along.
Early access: play with people you know, keep your own saves, and report problems on GitHub.
Publish.ChangeLog: 0.3.10: The Multiplayer button at the top of the right-hand column now opens the panel when you click it. The game switches mouse input off for that whole column and only its own buttons switch it back on; this mod's button never did, so it was drawn but every click went straight through into the city. It now uses the game's own right-menu styling, the same as the Chirper button, and switches mouse input on for itself. 0.3.9: Fixes the null reference in SerializerSystem during a save to the server, which both of us hit. The upload deleted the save you were playing and then saved over it, while the game still had that save's data open; the save failed part way and left the serializer broken. It now saves over the slot exactly the way the game's own Save and Quick Save do. The automatic save to the server runs at most every five minutes (it never ran at all before 0.3.4, so a short setting that used to do nothing would now stall the host). When a shared city has Road Builder roads that are new on your PC, the city now loads once more by itself instead of Road Builder asking you to reload it. And the in-game panel, the syncing box and the player markers are attached reliably again: 0.3.8 asked the game whether it offered each slot first, and after the interface reloaded the game wrongly said no, so they were left out. 0.3.8: The in-game panel is back, and the Syncing world box finally does what it says. This game version does not offer the toolbar slot the round button used to live in, so the button was never created at all, and with no button there was no way to open the panel: that is why it looked as though the panel did not exist. The button is now pinned over the game view, bottom right. The Syncing world box was only a picture: the game's tools do not take notice of it, so everyone carried on building through a sync and that work was then wiped by the save that arrived. During a sync every player now really is held, and gets their tool back afterwards. If the mod is installed twice, once from Paradox Mods and once as a local copy, the game mixes the two and the panel and the box stop appearing; the mod now spots that and tells you, in the panel, on the Options page and in the log. The panel, the menu screen and the Options page now show the same one line about how your city is doing, plus a tally of every build that has arrived, so they can no longer disagree. 0.3.7: Closes a hole opened by the retries in 0.3.6. When another player's build was put back to be tried again, the pieces the game had already made from it were left lying in your city with nothing owning them, and your game could then send them out again as though you had built them. That is the old "it is placing things for my friend" fault, and it is now impossible: every path that abandons a build clears up after itself. 0.3.6: Your game no longer builds half of what someone else placed. When part of another player's build is not valid here, the whole thing is held and tried again for a few seconds, and only if it still will not go does it give up and say so. Before, the valid parts were built anyway, which left half a road or a building with no approach, and everything placed near it afterwards then collided with the mess. The panel and the log also now show a full tally of every build that has arrived: replayed, batched, part-built, retried, given up, waiting. The numbers add up, so a problem cannot hide. 0.2.3 to 0.2.9: first published build and the run-up to 0.3.0 — server window and shared city, live build sync, city settings and shared treasury, player markers, playset-aware mod check, Traffic Tool Essentials and Traffic and Road Builder settings syncing, tool ghosts, progression sync, and the New city / load-or-new-world flow.
